catalog_quote: Mano has three level tones, low (kɛ̀ɛ̀ ‘year’), mid (kɛ̄ ‘in order to’), and high (kɛ́í ‘refuse’). Extra-high tone is marginal in the system, as it appears only in ideophones, expressive adverbs, and interjections ... The tone-bearing unit is a vowel or a syllabic nasal; long vowels and diphthongs are considered combinations of phonemes. Complex tonal contours appear only on VV sequences. All tonal combinations are possible (see Table 3). Unlike some Southwestern Mande languages, such as Kpelle (Konoshenko 2014), no tonal spreading occurs in Mano, and grammatical tonal marking is hosted by specific words rather than phrases. Furthermore, Mano does not have stress accent, which is often (but not always) the case for tonal languages (Hyman 2009). Utterance-level prosodic operations include the lowering of the tone on final vowels in affirmative utterances and a general downdrift. || Mandenkan 54 (2015) p. 25 fn. 12: « Si une langue donnée est sans accent, le deuxième terme peut être préféré. Même si l’accent n’est pas une propriété structurante de la phonologie mano, il y a des données indirectes de l’asymétrie entre les voyelles au sein des structures à plus d’une voyelle: c’est notamment la réduction de la première voyelle dans les structures CV1lV1 (cf. §1.8), de la première voyelles dans certaines structures CV1V2 (1.2.7) » || Jazyki mira (2017) p. 682: « 2.1.2. Ударения в М.я. нет. »
world_status: statement found in an open source

PDF page 8 = journal p.129, sec. 3.2 'Suprasegmental phonology' contains, verbatim: 'Mano has three level tones, low (kɛ̀ɛ̀ 'year'), mid (kɛ̄ 'in order to'), and high (kɛ́í 'refuse').. Unlike some Southwestern Mande languages, such as Kpelle (Konoshenko 2014), no tonal spreading occurs in Mano, and grammatical tonal marking is hosted by specific words rather than phrases. Furthermore, Mano does not have stress accent, which is often (but not always) the case for tonal languages (Hyman 2009). Utterance-level prosodic operations include the lowering of the tone on final vowels in affirmative utterances…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mano is a three-level tone language (L/M/H, all contour combinations on vowel sequences, marginal extra-high) with no word stress/stress accent according to its describer; the only sub-word prosodic constituent is the 'metric foot' (V, CV(ŋ), CVV, CVCV(ŋ)), a domain of vowel harmony, consonant-distribution restrictions and grammatical tone replacement, not of prominence. The grammar notes only indirect within-foot asymmetry (the first vowel of CVlV / some CV1V2 feet may reduce in fast speech, i.e. if anything the non-initial vowel is the stable one).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None (no stress at all per source).
new_statements.exceptions: English loanwords in Liberian Mano keep the English stress pattern (deZeeuw & Kruah 1981); fast-speech reduction of the first vowel in CVlV feet (CVlV > ClV) noted as indirect vowel asymmetry (Khachaturyan 2015: 25 fn.12, §1.8).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word/lexical level; phrase-level prosody consists of downdrift and utterance-final tone lowering (affirmatives) and raised register/final rise in questions. Description based mainly on Guinean Mano (Nzérékoré area; Maa/Zan dialects), which the author treats as one language with Liberian Mano.
new_statements.identity_note: All three quoted statements are by the same describer (M. Khachaturyan) and rest primarily on Guinean Mano (máá, Nzérékoré prefecture; Maa, Zan/Yassédou dialects), which Glottolog subsumes under mann1248 'Mann' (ISO mev) together with Liberian Mano (Nimba County). deZeeuw & Kruah 1981 and Schwab 1947 describe Liberian Mano and say nothing about native word stress. No dialect-level glottocode distinction is needed; the language-level key mann1248 is correct.

new_statements.quote: p. 360: "While stress is generally non-contrastive in Mande it is generally distinctive. In Kpelle, it falls on the first high-toned syllable in the word, or if the word has no high tones, it falls on the first syllable. Stress is acoustically marked by an increase in the loudness of the syllable and is often accompanied by a slight increase in the length of the syllable." [...] "No Mande language has more than three distinctive pitch levels. Kpelle and Mano have three: high, mid and low, while Lorma and Manya have two." — front matter p. [vi]: "Loan words generally reproduce the stress pattern of the English word, so that if you simply pronounce the word with its ordinary stress it will sound all right."

In Kpelle, it falls on the first high-toned sylla-ble in the word, or if the word has no high tones, it falls on the first syllable. Kpelle and Mano have three: high, mid and low, while Lorma and Manya have two.' The puts this held by the project and maps leaf 372…
new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's existing statement (Khachaturyan 2021: 'Mano does not have stress accent'; 2017: 'Ударения в М.я. нет'): the handbook gives Mano no stress rule, treats word prosody as three level tones, and the Dwyer appendix calls Mande stress non-contrastive. It adds two details: English loanwords retain English stress, and a Mande-general phonetic prominence (loudness + length) is asserted, with placement stated only for Kpelle. It must not be read as a Mano placement rule; the Kpelle 'first high-toned syllable' rule is not claimed for Mano.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mano is presented as a three-level-tone language (high, mid, low; mid unmarked, with the mid-low interval small). The only stress statement is in Dwyer's Mande-general appendix: stress in Mande is 'generally non-contrastive' (a loudness/length prominence), and the placement rule given is for Kpelle (first high-toned syllable, else first syllable) — no placement rule is stated for Mano. The only Mano-specific remark on stress is that English loanwords keep their English stress pattern.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Mano. The appendix's 'generally distinctive' after 'generally non-contrastive' reads as a slip (presumably 'predictable'); the Kpelle rule is explicitly for Kpelle.
new_statements.identity_note: Dezeeuw & Kruah (1981) is based mainly on the 'lao maa' dialect (area west of Sacklepie north to Ganta, Nimba County, Liberia), with informants from other areas (introduction, 'Mano Dialects'); principal informant Rexanna Kruah of Yilah, Bong County. The stress paragraph itself is in David Dwyer's appendix on Liberian Mande languages generally and is illustrated with Kpelle, not Mano.

tone_statements.quote: Одностопный или многостопный характер лексемы определяет ее поведение при присоединении супрасегментных морфем: в неодностопной лексеме грамматическое изменение тона происходит только на последней стопе (см. тон в имперфективе, 2.1.4, тон в сопряженной конструкции, 2.1.5). [...] При образовании конструкции с МПП сопряженной серии используется форма глагола с низким тоном на последней стопе (подробнее о ее образовании см. часть 1.1.2.).
tone_statements.translation: The mono- or polypodal character of a lexeme determines its behaviour when suprasegmental morphemes are attached: in a lexeme of more than one foot the grammatical change of tone takes place only on the last foot (see tone in the imperfective, 2.1.4, tone in the conjoint construction, 2.1.5). [...] In the construction with predicative markers of the conjoint series the verb form with low tone on the last foot is used (for details of its formation see part 1.1.2).

tone_statements.quote: Le ton joue une fonction distinctive. Il est représenté par les signes suivants : – Le ton haut { ´ } Exemple : déin / qui – Le ton bas { ` } Exemple : dèin / bourgeon – Le ton neutre ou médiane { ¯ } Exemple : dēin / escargot – Le voyelle non-marqué Exemple : dein / suite
tone_statements.translation: Tone has a distinctive function. It is represented by the following signs: high tone { ´ } e.g. déin 'who'; low tone { ` } e.g. dèin 'bud'; neutral or mid tone { ¯ } e.g. dēin 'snail'; the unmarked vowel, e.g. dein 'continuation'.
tone_statements.locator: p. 7, section III 'L'alphabet et la phonologie', §2 'Le ton'
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 marked (high, low, mid/'neutre') plus an unmarked-vowel category

Труды Института лингвистических исследований VII(2). Санкт-Петербург: Наука. (pages not given in the record; online text shows page markers 306-323)
tone_statements.quote: Le verbe peut être doté des morphèmes segmentaux … et des morphèmes supra-segmentaux (marques tonales de la construction imperfective et de la construction conjointe; si le verbe a un pré-verbe ou s’il comporte plus d’un pied métrique2, le ton grammatical ne porte que sur le composant final ou le pied métrique final). … Le modèle du changement de ton de l’imperfectif tient à la classe tonale du verbe. … Tous les verbes dont la forme lexicale ne comporte que des tons bas sont réunis dans une seule classe tonale B, … B ton bas … H ton haut … M ton moyen
tone_statements.translation: The verb can carry segmental morphemes … and supra-segmental morphemes (tonal marks of the imperfective construction and of the conjoint construction; if the verb has a preverb or comprises more than one metric foot, the grammatical tone bears only on the final component or the final metric foot). … The pattern of imperfective tone change depends on the tonal class of the verb. … All verbs whose lexical form contains only low tones are grouped in a single tonal class B, … B low tone … H high tone … M mid tone
tone_statements.locator: p. 15, sec. 1.1.2 'Morphologie du verbe' (Tableau 1 tonal classes on p. 16); tone labels from 'Liste des abbréviations' pp. 52-53
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones, low, mid, high; verbs fall into lexical tonal classes (H, HH, M, MM, BH, BM, B); grammatical tone marks imperfective (lowered) and conjoint (final foot low) forms.

tone.quote: Le ton joue une fonction distinctive. Il est représenté par les signes suivants : – Le ton haut { ´ } Exemple : déin / qui – Le ton bas { ` } Exemple : dèin / bourgeon – Le ton neutre ou médiane { ¯ } Exemple : dēin / escargot – Le voyelle non-marqué Exemple : dein / suite

tone.translation: Tone has a distinctive function. It is represented by the following signs: high tone { ´ } e.g. déin 'who'; low tone { ` } e.g. dèin 'bud'; neutral or mid tone { ¯ } e.g. dēin 'snail'; the unmarked vowel, e.g. dein 'continuation'.
tone.n_tones: 3 marked (high, low, mid/'neutre') plus an unmarked-vowel category
tone.says: A short section 'Le ton' states that tone is distinctive and marks three tones - haut (´), bas (`), 'neutre ou médiane' (¯) - with the minimal set déin 'qui' / dèin 'bourgeon' / dēin 'escargot', plus an 'unmarked vowel' category (dein 'suite'); entries throughout are tone-marked. No analysis beyond this; consistent with the three-level system listed here (Khachaturyan).

sources.quote: Le verbe peut être doté des morphèmes segmentaux … et des morphèmes supra-segmentaux (marques tonales de la construction imperfective et de la construction conjointe; si le verbe a un pré-verbe ou s’il comporte plus d’un pied métrique2, le ton grammatical ne porte que sur le composant final ou le pied métrique final). … Le modèle du changement de ton de l’imperfectif tient à la classe tonale du verbe. … Tous les verbes dont la forme lexicale ne comporte que des tons bas sont réunis dans une seule classe tonale B, … B ton bas … H ton haut … M ton moyen
sources.locator: p. 15, sec. 1.1.2 'Morphologie du verbe' (Tableau 1 tonal classes on p. 16); tone labels from 'Liste des abbréviations' pp. 52-53
sources.note: Three level tones, low, mid, high; verbs fall into lexical tonal classes (H, HH, M, MM, BH, BM, B); grammatical tone marks imperfective (lowered) and conjoint (final foot low) forms.

tone.quote: Le verbe peut être doté des morphèmes segmentaux … et des morphèmes supra-segmentaux (marques tonales de la construction imperfective et de la construction conjointe; si le verbe a un pré-verbe ou s’il comporte plus d’un pied métrique2, le ton grammatical ne porte que sur le composant final ou le pied métrique final). … Le modèle du changement de ton de l’imperfectif tient à la classe tonale du verbe. … Tous les verbes dont la forme lexicale ne comporte que des tons bas sont réunis dans une seule classe tonale B, … B ton bas … H ton haut … M ton moyen
tone.locator: p. 15, sec. 1.1.2 'Morphologie du verbe' (Tableau 1 tonal classes on p. 16); tone labels from 'Liste des abbréviations' pp. 52-53
tone.translation: The verb can carry segmental morphemes … and supra-segmental morphemes (tonal marks of the imperfective construction and of the conjoint construction; if the verb has a preverb or comprises more than one metric foot, the grammatical tone bears only on the final component or the final metric foot). … The pattern of imperfective tone change depends on the tonal class of the verb. … All verbs whose lexical form contains only low tones are grouped in a single tonal class B, … B low tone … H high tone … M mid tone
tone.summary: Three level tones, low, mid, high; verbs fall into lexical tonal classes (H, HH, M, MM, BH, BM, B); grammatical tone marks imperfective (lowered) and conjoint (final foot low) forms.
tone.says: Three level tones, low, mid, high; verbs fall into lexical tonal classes (H, HH, M, MM, BH, BM, B); grammatical tone marks imperfective (lowered) and conjoint (final foot low) forms.

sources.note: The segment list of inventory GM 1518 contains exactly three tone segments - ˦ (high tone bar), ˧ (mid tone bar), ˨ (low tone bar) - alongside the consonants and vowels; i.e. a secondhand coding of a three-level tone system taken from Khatchaturyan 2009. (This is evidently the origin of en.wikipedia's tone figures.) Adds no analysis; useful only as a database cross-reference consistent with the statement listed here.

sources.citation: Khachaturyan [Khatchaturyan], Maria. 2011. Le système prédicatif du mano de Guinée. Mandenkan 47: 13-56. doi:10.4000/15z7g (HAL hal-01137443, record gives pp. 13-55).
sources.note: Verbal grammatical tones in Mande are mainly replacive, independent of segmental morphemes, form phonologically determined inflectional classes; Perfective/Irrealis GTs argued to go back to Proto-Mande. Any Mano content would concern its verbal grammatical tones (imperfective / conjoint low tone), not the lexical inventory.
